Q: what does the acrosome do in a sperm cell
A: "The acrosome is an organelle that develops over the anterior half of the head of sperm cells. It contains digestive enzymes, such as hyaluronidase and acrosin, which are crucial for breaking down the outer membrane of the ovum, known as the zona pellucida. This process allows the haploid nucleus in the sperm cell to join with the haploid nucleus in the ovum, facilitating fertilization. The shedding of the acrosome, known as the acrosome reaction, is essential for successful fertilization."

Q: what powers did the bantu education give the government
A: "The Bantu Education Act of 1953 provided the South African government with the power to consolidate and control the education of black South Africans. It established a centralized system for black education, which allowed the government to implement discriminatory educational practices uniformly across the country. The Act mandated racial segregation in education, ensuring that black students received significantly inferior educational resources compared to their white counterparts. This included a disparity in funding, with black education receiving only one-tenth of the resources allocated to white education. The government also controlled the curriculum and the administration of black education, reinforcing the apartheid system and limiting the opportunities available to black South Africans."
